A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Landscape of Thoughts framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning visualizations, quantitative metrics, verifier accuracy, test-time scaling, and transfer experiments across four datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds statistical analyses, tokenization robustness tests, process-verifier results, and reasoning-model case studies.

M1.justification: The visualization pipeline and original random-forest outcome verifier remain unchanged. Appendix D.4 adds a process-verifier variant that predicts whether individual states favor the correct answer, using current and preceding thoughts, then aggregates these predictions. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Both versions use AQuA, MMLU, StrategyQA, and CommonsenseQA with the same task coverage. The additional StrategyQA analyses and newer-model case studies use these retained tasks; Figures 25–27 explicitly use AQuA.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds the process-verifier alternative alongside the original outcome-verifier and no-verifier conditions. CoT, LtM (also called L2M), ToT, MCTS, and unweighted voting remain. The new discussion of external reward models does not establish that those cited methods were experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The stated budgets remain 50 test questions, 20 verifier-training questions per dataset, and 10 sampled paths. Targeted additions introduce sentence-splitting controls and convergence/landscape-similarity metrics. Appendix E also evaluates QwQ-32B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B/Qwen-1.5B configurations. No revision of the original benchmark protocol is established.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation: D.1 quantitatively examines visual observations; D.2 tests over-splitting and under-splitting thoughts; D.4 compares verifier variants; and D.5 investigates the StrategyQA anomaly across models and algorithms. Appendix E adds annotated self-evaluation and backtracking case studies for newer reasoning models.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 newly reports log-linear convergence estimation and p-values of 0.008 for correct/incorrect convergence differences and 9.421e-11 for the speed–accuracy association. v1 has no corresponding significance reporting. The significance-test designs are insufficiently specified, and no additional repeated-run or seed counts are disclosed.

E6.justification: The original benchmark plots and scores are retained. v2 adds convergence and similarity measurements in Table 1, absolute transfer accuracies in Table 2, process-verifier entries in Table 3, and robustness/diagnostic findings. Table 3 is labeled AQuA, although its no-verifier and outcome-verifier columns reproduce Figure 5’s four-dataset averages; these entries therefore cannot establish a same-setting AQuA performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly defines a convergence coefficient through log-linear regression and a bounded path-speed measure using endpoint displacement divided by cumulative path length. The original mathematical formulation, Equations 2.1–2.8 and 4.1, is retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central visualization, reasoning-observation, and verifier-adaptation claims and the three contribution bullets retain their meaning. The added abstract sentence highlights accuracy and test-time scaling benefits already claimed and demonstrated in v1 Section 4.2.

C2.justification: New discussions materially expand the interpretation and qualifications. B.2 explains aggregation advantages over manual text analysis. B.3 distinguishes inexpensive verifier training from landscape construction requiring n × c forward passes. D.5 attributes StrategyQA anomalies to model instability and unreliable feature estimation. The existing multiple-choice limitation remains.

D1.justification: C.1 specifies that the correct-answer distance occupies the first feature coordinate, elaborating v1’s fixed-coordinate alignment. D.2 discloses period-based splitting and the comma/merging controls; D.4 explains automatic state-label construction. These add implementation information. The code-access statement and original sampling budgets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B, Luo et al. (2024), and Xu et al. (2025), supporting newer-model examples and discussion of process-reward-model costs. Section 5 and the existing research positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained with local rewrites, expanded explanations, and updated cross-references. The appendices are reorganized: the Impact Statement moves to A, existing discussion becomes B.1, and settings and visualizations become C and E, alongside new analysis subsections.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with three tables, a tokenization comparison, four StrategyQA landscape figures, and three annotated reasoning-model figures. Existing Figures 1–7 retain their displays with caption/layout refinements; v1 Figures 8–19 are retained as v2 Figures 13–24.

improvement.justification: The tokenization controls in D.2 test a previously unexamined assumption, and B.3 clarifies the verifier’s training-versus-inference cost tradeoff, providing a modest net improvement in evaluating and using the tool. Gains are limited by new reporting problems: D.1 leaves significance-test details unclear and misassigns observation references, while Table 3’s AQuA label conflicts with values matching the retained four-dataset averages.
